clue.text: NI political party's upset Murphy

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the letters are turned upside down, so read from the bottom up

parts.note: the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland; with the 's it gives DUPS

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish party has annoyed someone called Murphy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns DUPS (the DUP, a Northern Ireland party, with its 's) upside down. Murphy is Irish-flavoured slang for a potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: a murphy is an informal word for a potato, from its association with Ireland.

clue.text: Friend took food for sense of taste

parts.note: a pal is a friend
ate means took food

explanation.surface: A companion ate for the sake of savouring flavours.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the roof of the mouth gives its name to one's sense of taste and discernment in flavour.

clue.text: Photograph of house in street

indicators.note: in places the house abbreviation inside the street abbreviation

explanation.surface: A picture of a home in a road, as an estate agent might take.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a shot is a single photograph or snap taken with a camera.

clue.text: Start to give official approval for pleasure

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, here of give

parts.note: ratification is formal official approval of a treaty or agreement

explanation.surface: An instruction to begin granting formal sanction in the name of enjoyment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to give' supplies only G; 'Start' looks like a verb meaning begin but is the first-letter signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: satisfaction or enjoyment, as in the instant kind of delight people seek.

clue.text: Playing badminton topless is coming to the fore

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are put into play and moved about
topless in a down clue removes the top, the first letter of badminton

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of a shirtless badminton player who is winning the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' drops the B of badminton, and 'Playing' rearranges the remaining ADMINTON.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something prevailing or taking precedence is the controlling, foremost element.

clue.text: Argue with cyclist crossing start of cycleway

indicators.note: crossing has the cyclist's word straddling the letter, so it goes around it

parts.note: a biker is someone who rides a bike

indicators.note: start of takes the opening letter of cycleway

explanation.surface: Having a row with a rider who cuts across the bike lane.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to squabble or quarrel over petty matters.

clue.text: Charm one's way in

definitions.meaning: as a verb stressed on the second syllable, to delight or bewitch
as a noun stressed on the first syllable, a door or gateway

explanation.surface: Someone talks their way inside by being charming.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are spelt alike but pronounced differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Homograph: one spelling is both a verb meaning to enchant and a noun for a doorway.

clue.text: A PC hero disturbed thief

indicators.note: disturbed letters are thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A heroic police constable has upset a burglar.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: one who steals game or fish from someone else's land is a kind of thief.

clue.text: Hunter of stars to take part in oratorio nonsense

indicators.note: take part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A star-gazer invited to perform in a silly choral work.
explanation.definitionFit: Mythology: the giant huntsman of Greek legend is a constellation, so a hunter made of stars.

clue.text: Queen featured in silly sketch

indicators.note: featured in places the queen's letter inside the word for silly

parts.note: daft means silly
R is from Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A monarch appears in a comic revue sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a preliminary version or outline of a piece of writing or drawing.

clue.text: One perhaps musing hours in mobile repairer

indicators.note: in puts the hours abbreviation inside the travelling mender

parts.note: a tinker was an itinerant mender of pots and pans

explanation.surface: Someone mulling things over for hours while working at a phone repair stall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile repairer' suggests a phone fixer; it is a travelling mender of pots.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: someone pondering or reflecting is an example of one who ponders deeply.

clue.text: Quiet force keeps returning fire for officer

indicators.note: keeps means the quiet-and-force pair holds the next part inside it

parts.note: SH is a call for quiet
F is the physics symbol for force

indicators.note: returning means the word fire is read backwards

explanation.surface: A peaceful police force keeps sending fire back at an officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' gives ERIF, and 'keeps' means the quiet-plus-force pair holds it; 'force' looks like the police but is the physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a county law-enforcement official in the US, or a ceremonial post in Britain.

clue.text: Token job is an indicator of one's direction of travel

definitions.text: indicator of one's direction of travel

parts.note: a sign is a token or indication
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: A nominal job taken as a sign of where one's career is heading.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a roadside pole bearing arms that point the way to places.

clue.text: Mischievous child wandered about and made progress

parts.note: an imp is a naughty child
roved means roamed or wandered about

explanation.surface: A naughty youngster roamed around and got better.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: got better or advanced, as a pupil's grades might.

clue.text: A professional needs new protective garment

parts.note: pro is short for professional

explanation.surface: A tradesman needs fresh workwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a cloth worn over the front of one's clothes to keep them clean while cooking.

clue.text: Set to become adult, losing weight

indicators.note: losing means the weight letter is taken out

parts.note: to grow up is to become adult

explanation.surface: Someone is poised to mature while slimming down.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a collection or category of things or people regarded together.

clue.text: Awful story about English seafood

indicators.note: about means the mangled letters go around the abbreviation
awful suggests the word story is badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A dreadful tale concerning English fish and shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges STORY to OYSTR, and 'about' wraps it round E.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a bivalve mollusc eaten raw is one kind of shellfish from the sea.

clue.text: Set small dwelling beside one Great Lake

parts.note: a cot is a small cottage
Lake Erie is one of the five Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: Install a little cabin next to a North American lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a small exclusive clique or circle of people with shared interests.

clue.text: Knee-jerk reaction about electric cable

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a flex is a flexible insulated electric cable on an appliance

explanation.surface: An unthinking response to a dispute over a power lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an involuntary response, the knee-jerk being the textbook test of one.

clue.text: Fool wears petulant expression to complete training

indicators.note: wears means the fool has the expression on, so the expression goes around it

parts.note: a pout is a sulky look
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: An idiot sulks as the end of the course approaches.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to graduate from a military or police training course is to finish it formally.

clue.text: Proposal made for unusually wrapping iron

indicators.note: wrapping means the rearranged letters go around the iron symbol
unusually says the word for is arranged in an unusual order

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A suggestion produced for pressing clothes in an odd way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' gives OFR, which 'wrapping' puts round the metal; 'iron' looks like pressing clothes but is the element.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a bid or suggestion put forward for acceptance.

clue.text: Drive off from Carnoustie

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the inside of the place name

explanation.surface: A tee shot at Carnoustie, the Scottish championship golf links.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive off' looks like a golf phrase, given the course; it means expel.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to expel or force someone out of a position.

clue.text: Scottish measure river fish

parts.note: an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A Scottish unit of length applied to a river fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'measure' here is the old word for a dance, not a unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a lively Scottish folk dance; measure is an archaic term for a dance.

clue.text: Took action against English leather company's product

parts.note: sued means took legal action against

explanation.surface: A lawsuit was brought against an English tannery over its goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a soft napped leather is one of the things a leather firm makes.

clue.text: Filthy outside broadcast location

parts.note: a scene is the location of an event

explanation.surface: A dirty site for a TV crew filming on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: offensively indecent or lewd, in the sense of dirty talk.
